answer.says: Shri Hegde, you speak of the tiffen shop as though it were the summit of history. It is a moment in the system of needs, nothing more. But I note your urgency; the body is the condition of the file's existence, and I am no longer in a position to lecture on the distinction. Ramesh, you have your concession. Do not let the fire die. The spirit of the household must not starve while the bureaucracy dreams.
answer.thought: The morning holds its breath in the haze, a suspended moment where the error of my name still hangs in the air like the particulate matter. I have secured the mediation of Ramesh's labor, though the cash in my pocket is a thin reed against the debt. Hegde's hunger is a practical argument I cannot refute with dialectics; he must go, and I must remain to watch the substance of this day coalesce from the thin air of Diwali.
